This analysis reveals a distinct separation between the physical Higgs boson's measured mass and the vacuum expectation value responsible for all other masses. By treating the former as an experimentally determined parameter and the latter as a theoretical choice, we perform a comprehensive study of tree-level mass relations assuming heavy fermions and a potentially light second-lightest scalar. Under the assumption of a single underlying symmetry—be it a global $U(1)$, $SU(2)$, or a discrete $Z_2$—operating above the electroweak scale, we identify specific constraints on these symmetries. Our findings indicate that $U(1)$ assignments are generally incompatible with the observed fermion hierarchy, whereas $Z_2$ parities align well with current data, particularly when the model predicts a dark matter candidate. Furthermore, we map the predicted regions for scalar discoveries at the 14 TeV LHC and the higher-energy collider prospects at a 100 TeV collider.
